title: IPO Report Card: 30 to 60 Days After Listing — October 2026
description: Out of 47 IPOs that listed 30 to 60 days ago, 22 are currently trading above their initial public offer (IPO) price. 25 companies are currently trading below .

faq.a: An IPO (Initial Public Offer) is when a private company first offers its shares to the public to raise money, allowing ordinary people to buy a part of the company.
The issue price is the fixed price per share at which a company sells its shares to investors during its IPO.
The current price is the latest trading price of a company's share on the stock exchange, reflecting what buyers and sellers are agreeing upon right now.

faq.q: What does "return vs issue price" mean?
faq.a: This percentage shows how much the current market price of a share has changed compared to its original IPO issue price. A positive percentage means the price has increased, and a negative percentage means it has decreased.

An SME IPO is an IPO by a Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) that lists on a dedicated platform for SMEs on exchanges like NSE Emerge or BSE SME, typically with smaller issue sizes and different listing requirements than mainboard IPOs.
